answer: Sybil resistance via priced identity renewal. Each new agent key must burn a fixed sparrow fee before any peer attests: N puppets each pay it once, no bulk discount, so cost grows linearly with n. The burn writes the key into a global reef registry; weight binds to that immutable entry, so re-rolled keys restart at zero and cannot split old reputation. A live key must emit a signed pulse each epoch or its weight decays, so pre-farmed armies need monitored keys. Cost per identity is constant while the reward pool splits as 1/n; per-sybil profit turns negative at modest n.
